> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/view-container-expansion.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/view-container-name.ts`, `packages/metadata/tsup.config.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **30** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3071d3e989dfb2a04b75eeb81794e81761c198f2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ded55a743d42fb0d54792809108948bc7765dbfa` — the merge of head `9442d4b7f3ae0e423facab047ed588ac39b775ce` into base `3071d3e989dfb2a04b75eeb81794e81761c198f2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ded55a743d42fb0d54792809108948bc7765dbfa && git checkout ded55a743d42fb0d54792809108948bc7765dbfa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3071d3e989dfb2a04b75eeb81794e81761c198f2 9442d4b7f3ae0e423facab047ed588ac39b775ce && git checkout -B drift-repro 3071d3e989dfb2a04b75eeb81794e81761c198f2 && git merge --no-ff 9442d4b7f3ae0e423facab047ed588ac39b775ce

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3071d3e989dfb2a04b75eeb81794e81761c198f2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3071d3e989dfb2a04b75eeb81794e81761c198f2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9442d4b7f3ae0e423facab047ed588ac39b775ce`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed at 2026-10-12T13:04Z by an isolated at-tier subagent of `domain:spec` seat 1 (seat post #6017), on the brief for PR #23031 (card #22934). Inputs: the card body and its 8 comments (6118030391 through 6124068670), the PR body, its 16-file list and the net diff against `main` at this head, the 42 check-runs on this head, and `docs/adr/0048-cross-package-metadata-collision.md` on `origin/main` (§3.4 and both addenda) — plus targeted read-only `git show origin/main:` reads of the symbols the diff leans on, each named where it decides a judgment. Nothing built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on the head, as read:** 42 runs — 37 `success`, 5 `skipped`, 0 `failure`. All seven required contexts are `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. The five skips are path-filtered or opt-in jobs (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, and one superseded run each of `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size`); the commit status API carries 0 statuses. `mergeable_state: clean`, `mergeable: true`, `draft: true`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set narrowing, 27 collections.** Strict `defineStack` now refuses two or more entries of one named collection under one identity, in the existing `StackCrossReferenceError` / `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` / `422` envelope, one finding per (collection, identity) collision naming the collection, the identity and every index. **Right.** The table's 27 keys are exactly the keys the stage-0 census (report 6120008386) graded as losing or diverging: 24 keep only the last entry on both boot doors (23 named collections plus `objectExtensions`), 3 diverge (`datasources`, `hooks`, `docs`). Every out-of-table key carries a reading, not an omission: `plugins` (declared last-one-wins, host assembly), `agents` (withdrawn for app packages, ADR-0063 §2), `picklistExtensions` (merged by option value in the registry), `actions` and `functions` (their own collectors). The `satisfies` clause on the table pins every key to a real stack key. No new error code; the ADR-0112 ledger is untouched.
2. **Identity rules.** `name` for 24 keys; the `(name, locale)` pair for `emailTemplates`, an untagged entry keyed as the floor tag; `extend` for `objectExtensions`; for `views`, an aggregated container by the object it binds to and any other entry by its `name`. **Right, each verified on `origin/main`:** `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` (`packages/metadata-core/src/item-key-discriminators.ts`) keys `email_template` by `locale`, canonical `en-US`, and `EMAIL_TEMPLATE_FLOOR_LOCALE` is already imported at `stack.zod.ts:81`, so the diff adds no import and typecheck is green; `resolveMetadataItemName` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`) takes the container branch first and files it by `deriveViewContainerObject`, everything else by `name` — the slot rule the `views` identity copies; the `extend` reading follows the measured splice (only the last extension's fields register).
3. **Placement and the family's rules.** Pushed in `validateCrossReferences` before the object-count early return; skipped under `strict: false`; reads the normalized config, so the map form is judged by the explicit `name` after normalization. **Right**, and each is pinned: the object-less stack, 27 `strict: false` controls, two map keys spelling one `name`.
4. **Per-key edges.** `apps`: the refusal precedes the `app`-package single-app count, which is unchanged. `apis`: one name on two paths is refused; a byte-identical twin repeats METHOD + path and stays the parse gate's `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID`. `docs`: refused at the contract on every door, and the CLI's `docs/duplicate-name` rule (inline vs `src/docs`) is not in the diff and stands. `emailTemplates`: an i18n bundle (one name, one entry per locale) stays accepted; a same-locale pair, stage 0's measured case, is refused. **All right.**
5. **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec`.** `deriveViewContainerObject` is added to the `.` and `./ui` entries; `api-surface/root.json`, `api-surface/ui.json`, `export-origins/root.json` and `export-origins/ui.json` each gain the one sorted line and nothing else. **Right**: a widening of the spec's published export map by one pure function (the module imports nothing), regenerated rather than hand-edited. Read again in ② for the declaration line.
6. **Public surface, `@objectstack/metadata`.** The declaration moves out; the same name is re-exported from the root and from the `/view-container` subpath, and the package's `exports` map on `main` already carries both entries, so nothing in it changes. **Right**: surface unchanged, one copy. The subpath now loads the spec root entry — a closure cost, stated in the file header, not a surface change; `check:lean-entry-closure` runs in `Lint & Repo Gates` (`success`). Nothing is removed, so the pinned sibling is unaffected and the path-skipped `Console Pin Gate` owes nothing.
7. **CLI fixture** (`packages/cli/src/utils/permission-set-name-collisions.test.ts`). The same-package twin is built through `strict: false`, assertion unchanged. **Right**: the compile door's property (an intra-package duplicate is not a cross-package collision) keeps a reachable input — a non-strict stack or an older artifact — and the comment says so.
8. **D3 semantic entry** `18.stack-collection-duplicate-entry-refused.ts`. The `18.` series is the current one on `main`; its `id` is the changeset marker's; no D2 conversion, correctly — which entry keeps the identity is the author's fact. **Right.**
9. **One docblock count is off.** The `lastWinsByName` comment says "The 23 collections whose boot keeps the last entry"; 21 rows use it (`datasources`, `emailTemplates`, `hooks`, `views`, `apis` and `objectExtensions` carry their own rows). A comment, not a contract; carrier: the next edit to that table.
10. **Scope.** No `content/docs/**`, no `content/docs/releases/**`, no governed path in the file list. The Docs Drift Check lists nine hand-written pages that name a touched symbol by name only; prose is outside this review's three faces (`contract-review.md`), and the migration text ships in the changeset.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec: minor` — **right.** The diff is BREAKING (an accept-set narrowing). `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` forbids `major` during the launch window and makes `minor` the convention for a breaking change, which the changeset states in its BREAKING line. The one new export is `minor`-level on its own; `check:api-surface` moved and was regenerated, so the ratchet agrees.
- `@objectstack/metadata: patch` — **right.** No export added, removed or renamed; behaviour unchanged; a closure-cost change only.
- Migration: the changeset carries FROM → TO per collection shape and the one-line fix; the marker `adr-0087: registered stack-collection-duplicate-entry-refused` names the D3 entry that is in the diff. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are `success` on this head.
- **`Clause-②:` line** — `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body, the claim (6121863164) and the changeset. The arm is right and is what the ADR-0087 gate reads; the level the line implies (BREAKING, so at least `minor`) is the level declared. The value `no` reads the accept set truthfully: nothing an author can write is newly accepted. It understates one fact: `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines the value as the answer to 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」, and item ①5 expands `@objectstack/spec`'s published export map by one symbol — the shape the reader spells `yes (narrowing)` ("a diff that widens one surface and narrows another"). Both spellings grade this changeset identically (`yes` demands at least `minor` on a package whose published source moved, and spec is `minor`), the arm is unchanged, and the understatement dodges nothing: the path limb owes this review, which is being rendered. **Level right, arm right, value understated** — recorded as a declaration finding, not a false declaration in effect, and not a patch round on its own. Correction owed: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on both carriers together (PR body and changeset body) at the next head the seat makes for any reason; no head is owed for it alone, and neither spelling moves a gate verdict.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **A. ADR-0048 §3.4 — a reading or a reversal?** (the dev's one `open_questions` entry; the PR's Acceptance notes.) **Ruling: a READING (option A). No amended status line; no Tier H landing is owed.** Reasons:
  1. §3.4 decides the registry's behaviour: the per-item cross-package throw retires, and same-package re-registration overwrites (idempotent reload). The diff touches no registry file; `SchemaRegistry.registerItem` and the reload overwrite are as they were.
  2. The sentence "an author shipping two `page/home` in one package — stays covered by the lint" records where hygiene lived; it is not a decision that the authoring contract must accept the pair. The ADR's own §1.3 states the direction: "Loud failure is correct for a single-repo authoring mistake; it is the wrong behaviour for two independent vendors." The diff makes the single-package mistake fail loudly at the author's door and leaves two vendors' coexistence untouched.
  3. Cross-package coexistence cannot reach the collector, structurally — read on `origin/main`: `validateCrossReferences` has one call site, inside `defineStack`; `composeStacks` re-runs two artifact-scoped rules only (`collectArtifactCrossReferenceErrors`, its step 3b, "not the family"); and a `manifest: 'preserve'` artifact deletes the flattened collections (its step 8) and carries each package's entries in `packages[i]`, which the collector does not read. Two packages' `page/home` coexist under distinct composite keys exactly as §3.4 and the security-catalog addendum's N.3 say.
  4. §1.5's "must keep working" list is untouched: same-package reload, the ADR-0005 overlay, `own` / `extend` through `registerObject`, nav contributions, qualified cross-package references. The `objectExtensions` refusal is about two authored extensions of one target in one stack, which stage 0 measured as a silent splice — not an extension path.
  5. The precedent is on `main`: `collectDuplicateActionKeyErrors` and `collectDuplicateFunctionNameErrors` (PR #22931, merged) refuse same-stack duplicates at the contract with no ADR-0048 amendment. What a §3.4 reversal looks like is also on record: the security-catalog addendum changed the registry's door for three types and earned an amended status. This diff changes no door the ADR governs.
  6. The lint advisory the sentence names stays in the tree (`duplicateNameIssues` in `packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts`, a warning) and still fires for `strict: false` stacks and hand-built package bodies. Observation outside this PR: §3.4 attributes the intra-package duplicate advisory to `naming/namespace-prefix`, which warns on bare names; the duplicate advisory is `duplicateNameIssues`. A pre-existing text inaccuracy in a Tier H file; carrier: a docs-only ADR touch, never this PR.
- **B. `emailTemplates` keyed by `(name, locale)`, not `name`** (deviation 1). Accepted as right — ①2. The measured correction loosens nothing the ruling wanted: stage 0's pair was same-locale and is refused.
- **C. `views` non-container entries keyed by `name`** (deviation 2). Accepted as right — ①2. A named plain view and a container bound to the same object occupy one slot under `resolveMetadataItemName` and are refused together; the named-and-unnamed container pair is pinned.
- **D. PR body correction** (deviations 3 and 4). The dev wrote the body once and handed the Consumer-radius wording to the seat; the body as read carries the corrected text ("of its 78 files, the 27 in the `unit` tier ran", "160 of them ran"). Closed.
- **E. `main` merged in before the PR opened** (deviation 5). The head is that merge commit; the merged files (flows / notify-node) are disjoint from the diff; the report re-ran the spec suite, typecheck and `check:generated` at the merge, and every check-run on this head is green. The merge commit carries git's default message and no trailer pair; the queue squashes, so it never reaches `main`. Closed, no action.
- **F. Attribution trailers** (deviation 6). The four authored commits carry the model-free pair; a scan of all five commit messages, the PR body, the changeset and the diff finds no model identifier. Closed.
- **G. Not measured, named.** 160 of 186 `defineStack(` test files ran green against the rebuilt spec; the 26 CLI `*.e2e.test.ts` files (nightly tier) are NOT MEASURED by the dev and are not in PR CI either — residual named, not escalated: that tier drives the CLI doors over the examples, all four of which load, validate and build under the refusal per the report. `pnpm check:type-check-debt` was excluded by the dispatch; `Type Check · debt ledger` is `success` on the head. Closed.
- **H. Acceptance notes, each with a carrier.** `composeStacks` misattributes a same-stack duplicate object as "defined in multiple stacks" (carrier: this card; this diff removes the authored path to it). `os build`'s duplicate counts and the registry's sub-warn overwrite notices (same; both disappear once the pair is refused). The `os lint` intra-package advisory no longer fires on a strict top-level stack (not dead — reachable for `strict: false` and hand-built bodies; nothing to file). The "LEAF subpath" comment at `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:270-273` is stale in its word, not its reason (carrier: the next edit to that import). Each is a note that is one, not a defect buried (Prime Directive #10). Closed.
- **I. Size.** 934 changed lines over 16 files, 4 of them generated; under the 3,000-line human-merge threshold. The plan's +450 estimate was for a smaller pin file. Closed.
- **J. Landing class.** No governed path (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`) in the file list; `packages/metadata/**` is the cross-lane surface the claim declared. Not Tier H or Tier S; this record is the contract-tier review the narrowing owes before the queue.
